chunks: Among what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband has intercourse with her, then she menstruates before performing ghusl. He said: “If she wishes to perform ghusl, she may do so, and if she does not do so, there is nothing upon her. Then when she becomes pure, she performs one ghusl for menstruation and janābah.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of janābah caused by sexual intercourse
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا شَيْءٌ: there is no obligation or liability upon her

ai.seo_question: If a woman menstruates before performing ghusl from janābah, does she need one ghusl or two?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who enters menstruation before performing ghusl after janābah. It states that performing ghusl before the end of menstruation is optional, and after becoming pure she may suffice with a single ghusl for both ḥayḍ and janābah.
